_comment: Copy this file to <your-submission-folder>/submission.json and fill it in -- or just run `cbench community-package --model <tag> --accept-terms`, which writes the whole thing for you. Every field except _comment, _*_comment and notes is required; cbench community-validate refuses a submission missing any of them.
_model_comment: The exact tag your endpoint calls this model, verbatim -- the same string every CSV filename in this submission must contain (cbench community-validate checks this).
_date_comment: The date you ran these trials, not the date you opened the PR.
hardware_summary: e.g. RTX 4080 16GB VRAM, 64GB system RAM, Windows 11
_endpoint_comment: Runtime and version -- sampling defaults and quant handling differ between runtimes and versions, and this is exactly the kind of thing ARCHITECTURE.md's own "how not to fool yourself" section warns can confound a comparison.
cbench_version: output of `pip show openllm-cbench`, or the git commit hash you ran from
notes: Optional free text -- anything unusual about the run: a config_overrides you had to set, a caveat this model needed, trials you excluded and why, etc.
_checksums_comment: Written automatically by `cbench community-package`: SHA-256 per CSV, relative posix paths. Optional for a hand-assembled submission, but if present every entry must match, and every CSV present must be listed -- a mismatch means the file changed after packaging.
_policy_comment: RAW DATA ONLY. A submission must NOT contain a grade, score, band or rate field, and must not include a scorecard or trial_summary file -- validation refuses both. Anyone who wants a grade computes it from these CSVs with `cbench score --from-existing`. See community-results/README.md, 'The publication rule'.
_gate_check_comment: Written automatically from your local catalogue by `cbench community-package`. `unverified` MUST be empty: a gate check that timed out is an absent check, not a failed one, and rows produced on that machine may measure the machine rather than the model. Run `cbench gate --model <tag> --save` first.
_attestation_comment: Recorded by `--accept-terms` (or the TUI checkbox). You confirm you have the right to share these files, that they contain nothing confidential (having read the raw CSVs), that the recorded hardware and model tag are accurate, that you grant an Apache-2.0 licence to publish them, and that publication is permanent in git history.
